'''Nari Nari''' is an extinct [[Indigenous Australian language|Indigenous Australian]] dialect of [[Wemba Wemba language|Wemba Wemba]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.3 - Nari Nari |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/nari1241 |access-date=2026-03-07 |website=glottolog.org}}</ref> once spoken in [[New South Wales]]. The last person who could speak Nari Nari was Angus Myers, a [[Jitajita]] man.'''<ref name=":0">{{Citation |last=Hercus |first=Luise A. |title=A Note on Narinari |date=1979 |work=Papers in Australian Linguistics 11 |volume=51 |pages=119–132 |url=http://hdl.handle.net/1885/144561 |access-date=2026-03-07 |series=Pacific Linguistics: Series A |place=Canberra |publisher=Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, Australian National University |doi=10.15144/PL-A51}}</ref>''' It was last recorded in 1967, but date of extinction is unknown.

== Revival ==
{{as of|2020}}, the Nari Nari dialect<ref name="AIATSISD9">{{cite web |date=26 July 2019 |title=D9: Nari Nari |url=https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/d9 |access-date=14 January 2020 |website=Austlang |publisher=AIATSIS}}</ref> is one of 20 languages prioritised as part of the Priority Languages Support Project being undertaken by First Languages Australia and funded by the [[Department of Communications and the Arts]]. The project aims to "identify and document critically-endangered languages—those languages for which little or no documentation exists, where no recordings have previously been made, but where there are living speakers".<ref>{{cite web |title=Priority Languages Support Project |url=https://www.firstlanguages.org.au/projects/plsp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210224021102/https://firstlanguages.org.au/projects/plsp |archive-date=24 February 2021 |access-date=14 January 2020 |website=First Languages Australia}}</ref>
